title: feat(body-exposure): render a DICOM series in 3D, not a description of one
abstract:
The panel explained the DICOM → 3D pipeline and ran none of it. I wrote that sentence myself in #1562, called it *"engineering work, not wording"* — and then went back to wording. This is the engineering.

## What is new

| file | what it does |
|---|---|
| `src/lib/volumeTekstur.ts` | turns the existing `VolumeMpr` into a 3D texture — quantised into the chosen window, integer-downsampled when an axis exceeds 256, **physical size in millimetres carried separately** |
| `src/components/VolumeDicom3D.tsx` | ray-casts it on the GPU: WebGL2, GLSL3, `sampler3D`, slab-clipped rays, up to 512 steps, front-to-back compositing, orbit controls |
| `src/pages/bodyhub/VolumeDicomBagian.tsx` | picks files, decodes with the existing `bacaDicom`, stacks with `buatVolumeMpr`, exposes **lower and upper thresholds in Hounsfield units** |

## Two things that make such a render convincing and wrong

**Voxels are not cubes.** CT slice spacing is commonly millimetres while pixel spacing is under one, so a 64×64×24 stack drawn as a cube flattens the body along the head–foot axis. The box is proportioned by millimetres — in the test series the slice axis has the **fewest voxels (24)** and is physically the **longest (72 mm)**.

**One byte is not a thousand Hounsfield units.** What is mapped to 0–255 is the chosen window, and the window travels with the texture, so a slider labelled HU means HU.

Ray-casting rather than isosurface, deliberately: an isosurface discards the volume, and a hole in it cannot be told apart from a hole in the threshold you picked.

## Measured, not asserted

I built a synthetic uncompressed CT series — 24 slices, 64×64, a **700 HU sphere in −1000 HU air**, explicit VR little endian — and drove the real page at **390×844**.

```
parsed slices: 24 · modality CT
volume 64×64×24 · spacing 0.7 / 0.7 / 3 mm
box reported 45 × 45 × 72 mm · window −1000..700 HU
canvas: 22,978 lit pixels — 9.3% of it — brightest 238
```

The sphere renders. The rings visible on the screenshot are the 3 mm slice spacing — an artefact of the data, not of the renderer.

## A gate of mine that passed when it should have failed

`pencitraan-tak-saling-membantah.mts` asserted the boundary line *"This panel loads no study"* was **present**. Today the panel began loading studies, the sentence became false — and the gate stayed green. It pinned **wording instead of truth**, which is the exact defect class the rest of these gates hunt, sitting inside one of the gates.

It now reads whether the panel mounts a loader that calls `bacaDicom`, and requires the claim to match **in both directions**. Sabotage-proved on that specific miss:

```
S1 restore 'panel loads no study' while the panel does load
   → the panel now reads DICOM files, but a boundary statement still says it does not
S2 loader mounted but never reads DICOM
   → it claims to render a study it does not read
S3 loader unmounted but no boundary says so
   → the panel loads nothing, yet no boundary statement says so
```

`scripts/uji/volume-tekstur.mts` is sabotage-proved seven ways, including **proportioning the box by voxel count** (the flattening bug) and removing the ray-march loop. It recomputes the geometry independently — and caught my own arithmetic again: I expected 0.45, the correct ratio is **0.448**.

`npm run uji` **291/291**, `tsc --noEmit` clean, `npm run build` clean.

## Not claimed

Not a diagnostic workstation. No isosurface or mesh export yet. MRI thresholds are raw stored values and are **labelled as such**, because MRI intensity is not calibrated in HU. The KaloLumen licence remains `unresolved` — nothing of theirs is bundled, called or copied.
